title: Inspecting CSS
summary: A tour of Chrome DevTools for CSS: opening the inspector, the Elements and Styles panes, live editing, overridden (struck-out) rules, the Computed tab and CSS Overview. Ends with a four-question quiz on a practice site where answers are found with the inspector.

concepts.heading: Opening DevTools
points: Chrome only (the course assumes Chrome so everyone sees the same tools). Menu: three-dots, More tools, Developer tools.
Shortcuts: Cmd+Option+I on Mac, Ctrl+Shift+I on Windows, or F12 on many keyboards. The menu shows the exact shortcut for your machine.
Right-click any element and choose Inspect: opens DevTools and selects that element in the HTML.
The element-picker (arrow icon at the top-left of DevTools) lets you click an item on the page and jump to its HTML.

concepts.heading: Elements tab and Styles pane
points: The Elements tab shows the live DOM. The Styles pane beside it lists every CSS rule that applies to the selected element.
Browsers give every element default styles (the user-agent stylesheet). Turning the site's CSS off shows only these defaults.
Your own rules appear above the defaults, labelled with the file and line they came from (e.g. styles.css); clicking the label opens that source.

When two rules set the same property, the later/more specific one wins and the loser is shown struck through. Example: an anchor's default blue colour is crossed out because the site sets white. Unticking the site rule re-activates the default.

concepts.heading: Live editing is temporary
points: Use the + button in the Styles pane to add a declaration to the selected element, e.g. color: black on an h1; the page updates instantly.
Each declaration has a checkbox (or crossing control) to toggle it off and on to compare.

Nothing you do in DevTools changes the source files or the real site. It only changes the copy loaded in your browser and disappears on reload. Editing a big site's text this way does not alter that site or other users' views.
Workflow: experiment in DevTools, then copy the rules you like into your own stylesheet.
Confirm by opening the file in the Sources tab: the new rule is not there.

concepts.heading: Computed tab
points: Computed shows the final resolved values for the element in one flat list, hiding crossed-out noise. For example the link colour appears as an rgb(red, green, blue) value.
Useful for inherited properties: a paragraph's font-family may not be set on the p at all but inherited from body or html, and Computed still shows the value in use.
(Extra) In the Styles pane, inherited rules appear under an 'Inherited from ...' heading.

concepts.heading: CSS Overview
points: Open the DevTools own three-dots menu (not Chrome's), More tools, CSS Overview, then press Capture overview.
It summarises the page's background colours, text colours, fonts (font families in use) and more (media queries and unused declarations are skipped for now).
Handy for studying sites you like: find which colours and fonts they use and copy the values.

task.name: CSS inspection quiz
task.starting_point: Open the practice site at appbrewery.github.io/css-inspection/ in Chrome. It has an h1, an h2 and a paragraph, plus four answer fields and a Submit button.
task.goal: Use DevTools to find four CSS values and submit them to see if each is correct.
steps: Inspect the body and read its background colour (named colour).
Inspect the h1 and read its font-size.
Inspect the h2 and read its font-weight.
Inspect the paragraph and find its font-family. It is inherited, so look in the inherited section of Styles or switch to the Computed tab.
Type each answer into its field and press Submit.

solution_code.code:
body background-color: aliceblue
h1 font-size: 3rem
h2 font-weight: 500
p font-family: Arial, sans-serif (inherited; visible in Computed)

pitfalls: Expecting DevTools edits to be saved; they are lost on reload and never touch the real file.
Confusing Chrome's three-dots menu with DevTools' own three-dots menu when looking for CSS Overview.
Looking only at the paragraph's own rules and missing a font-family that is inherited.
Reading crossed-out declarations as active; the struck-through one is overridden.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (s06.js has colours, fonts, box model and the meme project only).
gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'Inspecting CSS': blurb about DevTools as a way to read any site's CSS, with 3-5 tasks: open the inspector on the playground preview, find an element's colour, toggle a declaration off, add a temporary rule, read an inherited font-family in Computed.
Starter code: a small page with a body background, an h1 with font-size in rem, an h2 with font-weight, and a p inheriting font-family from body, mirroring the quiz.
Interactive demo idea: a fake 'Styles pane' beside a sample element with checkboxes that toggle declarations live and show overridden ones struck through; plus a Computed list of final values.
